inputs.label: Right Flipper Button and Advance Input

physical.notes: PinMAME's flipper column for the right cabinet button. It drives the synthetic flipper outputs 45/46 while the game is on and is copied to matrix 16, where the cabinet sheet wires the RIGHT ADVANCE BUTTON. The physical button closes the RIGHT FLIPPER BUTTON contact that feeds the 20095 flipper coil from the Q relay's switched +24 V (folio 42). The advance button is a separate cabinet contact: folio 49 lists the two flipper switch assemblies (item 9, 17838-3) apart from two black pushbuttons with their own holders and switches (item 26, 23503 and 24293Y), and no page puts an advance contact on a flipper button. Only PinMAME's FLIP_SWNO(6,16) couples the two.

mechanisms.behavior: A kick-out hole at the upper right. A ball closes switch 76; outside multiball the ROM keeps it (CAPTURE BALL IF NOT IN MULTI-BALL), raises the Stargate ramp and releases the second ball from the trough, starting two-ball multiball. When the Stargate spot target is hit the ROM drops relay S and fires solenoid 3, kicking the captured ball out, and lowers the ramp. In multiball the hole scores the multi-bonus and kicks the ball straight back out. Solenoid 3 kicks only with relay S released; with S energized it flashes the Stargate bulbs instead.
mechanisms.label: Hole (Ball Capture)

mechanisms.behavior: A ramp at the upper left whose free end the 17875 coil lifts while lamp 14 is on and lets drop when it goes off; an end-of-stroke ON RAMP SW. (not on the matrix) switches the coil to its hold winding, and a separate normally open ON RAMP SW. lights the uncontrolled Stargate LAUNCH ATTACK lamp. Lowered, the ramp carries the ball up to the Stargate rollunder (71); raised, the ball passes under it to the Stargate spot target (72). The factory drawing of the assembly shows the levers upright and the free end level with the bracket when activated, and leaning with the end about a bracket height lower when deactivated. The ROM raises it when the hole captures a ball and lowers it when the spot target releases that ball; the table moves its ramp the same way from lamp 14. At game start the ROM raises it for under a second and lowers it again, so play starts with the ramp down; it also raises it at tilt.
mechanisms.label: Stargate Ramp

positions.description: Ball rides the ramp to the Stargate rollunder.
positions.label: Ramp lowered (lamp 14 off)

positions.description: Ball passes under the ramp to the Stargate spot target.
positions.label: Ramp raised (lamp 14 on)

mechanisms.behavior: Two balls. A drained ball closes outhole switch 66 and solenoid 9 kicks it into the trough. Trough switch 56 is closed only while both balls are in the trough; lamp driver 2 pulses the ball-release coil to feed one ball to the shooter lane, where it rolls over switch 36 and is plunged by hand. Start a game with 56 closed. The ROM counts the end of a ball when 56 closes again with both balls home.

The ROM's relay test turns Q on and holds it into the solenoid test, while it pulses T, the ball release (lamp 2), S, A and the Stargate ramp (lamp 14) one at a time (service sweep, 41.5-62.1 s).
